summary: The note explains how phishing scams have grown in frequency and sophistication as remote work expanded, covering tactics like spear-phishing, smishing and deepfakes. It describes the psychological principles phishers exploit (emotion, authority, reciprocation, commitment) and defenses including simulated attacks, AI detection tools, individual vigilance, security culture and emotional intelligence training. It also urges applying these habits to personal digital communications.
one_line: Phishing scams are rising with remote work, exploiting psychological tactics, and are countered by training, AI detection, vigilance and a security-aware culture.
key_facts: The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center reported a 300% increase in reported phishing incidents since remote work became prevalent.

On October 10, 2023, cyber intelligence firm WebSafe Shield released a report on the most common phishing tactics, including deceptive emails and websites, spear-phishing, and 'smishing' (phishing via text messages).
Dr. James Cameron, lead author of the WebSafe Shield report, warned that 'deepfake' technology is being used to create highly convincing video and audio content.
On November 15, 2023, a massive phishing campaign targeted several Fortune 500 companies, prompting expert Maria Gonzales to say "It's often the small details that give phishers away."
A National Cyber Security Alliance study published September 5, 2023 found the most effective phishing emails tap into emotions such as fear, curiosity, or a sense of urgency.
Phishers also exploit the principles of authority, reciprocation, and commitment to persuade victims to act against their own interest.
Behavioral psychologist Daniel Rogers said on September 20, 2023 that scammers pose as high-ranking officials or recognizable brands to leverage the authority principle.
On December 1, 2023, security analysts noted a scam where victims were first asked to confirm contact information, gradually leading to requests for company data.
On October 25, 2023, trainer Rebecca Liu ran a simulation for a large tech company that produced a 40% click rate on a dummy phishing link.

CyberShield Analytics touts AI-powered detection systems that predict and intercept phishing messages; CEO Jonathan Miller said on November 7, 2023 that the AI "learns from every attack, constantly improving the defensive measures."
David Patel, speaking on September 14, 2023, urged a 'pause and verify' approach: "slow down, scrutinize every communication, and verify its authenticity through a separate channel if necessary."
Linda Schmidt of NexGen Security said on December 12, 2023 that "an empowered team is the best defense against phishing attempts."
Emotional intelligence workshops and training are being incorporated into security training programs to bolster workers' psychological defenses.
